steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain. Keep warm.

Meanwhile, heat olive oil and butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add garlic; cook and stir until softened. Mix in eggplant. Let eggplant cook for 5 minutes without stirring. Then stir and cook until tender, about 5 more minutes.

Mix in spinach and season with salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3 minutes. Stir in drained pasta and lemon juice along with 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese. Transfer to a serving dish and top with remaining cheese and cracked black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta Melanzana
raw_recipe.description: Pasta melanzane is a quick and flavorful way to cook eggplant. This is a tasty one-dish meal that’s prepared with spinach and Parmesan cheese.
raw_recipe.name: Pasta Melanzana

review.reviewBody: This was quite good. An interesting cominbation of flavors. As suggested by a previous reviewer, I used 5 cups chopped spinach. Another change I made was to "sweat" the eggplant before cooking. I find that I do not like the taste of eggplant unless I sweat it first. To do this, slice the eggplant into about 1/2 inch slices, sprinkle both sides of each slice generously with salt, and let sit for at least an hour. The eggplant should release a fair amount of liquid. When ready to cook, rinse off the eggplant slices and pat dry.

it was easy and fast to make with great results-we all liked it! I added some hot pork sausage which I fried with the garlic and oil in the first step along with half an onion. My pasta choice was a package of ricotta and spinach ravioli. Super recipe and I will make this again! Great new way to use eggplant. Yum

The only reason that I didn't give it 5 stars is the way the ingredient amounts are listed. Dry pasta is more accurately measured by weight than volume...that is the amount of dry bowties that fit in a measuring cup is not the same as the amount of a more bulky shape, whereas 2 oz of pasta is considered a serving regardless of shape. Also, measuring fresh spinach by the cup is super inexact... better to say use a whole package of baby spinach [which weighs 5 oz but would probably be way more than 3 cups]. It's also not necessary to chop it, just remove the stems. That being said, it's a super easy and flexible recipe. The first time I used frozen chopped spinach and it was fine, but I think the fresh spinach works better. I also added some onion with the garlic [I love onion], and I happened to have a beautiful sweet red pepper in my garden, so I added strips of that which really added another layer of color and flavor. The last time I made it I added some chopped proscuitto for a little protein boost. It was wonderful each time. I might try adding some grilled chicken at the end next time.

So delicious! But... it definitely needs tweaking in the ingredient amounts. 3/4 cup of farfalle pasta only makes about 1 1/4 cups cooked pasta, not even close to being enough for 4 servings. I ended up having to cook more pasta to bulk things up. I think I ended up using about 2 cups dry pasta. The rest of the ingredient amounts are pretty accurate. Such bright, refreshing flavors, not heavy at all and suitable even on a hot summer day. We loved this and I will be making it again. I do recommended sweating the eggplant with a bit of salt, and letting it sit about 15 minutes before blotting off the excess liquid.
So. I actually haven't made this yet but gave it 5 stars because it looks delicious! My question is what can be substituted for the eggplant as we aren't fans of it?

My store had spinach and eggplant on sale, so I did an ingredient search and this recipe came up! It's a great use of eggplant. I did like another reviewer and "sweated" the eggplant. I used a microwave method I just read about in Cook's Illustrated (mix 1 cubed eggplant with 1 tsp kosher salt, line a plate with 2 layers of coffee filters and spray with cooking spray, microwave on high for 10 minutes, stirring halfway through). I left the skin on the eggplant and I used 6 cups of spinach because it cooks down so much. I used whole wheat rotini and threw in a handful of toasted pine nuts. Very tasty!

My boyfriend and I LOVE spinach, so we used 6 cups. I did sweat the eggplant first for about 30 minutes. I added the garlic to the eggplant after the first 5 minutes of cooking to make sure it didn't burn. I used 2 tablespoons of lemon juice, and it was perfectly lemony but a little dry. So I added about 1/2 cup of pasta water.

This dish is fantastic. We'll be making this very often!
A drizzle of fresh basil pesto or lemon zest to finish is traditional and will bring the needed brightness to this dish

This was good. I followed the advice of other reviewers and let the eggplant sweat for 1 hour prior to cooking it. The eggplant was not bitter at all. I added about 3 1/2 cups of spinach--I probably would add more next time. The dish has a great lemon flavor--the flavors come together nicely!

This was tasty. After reading the other reviews, I also added an onion and sweated the eggplant before cooking it. Due to cholesterol issues, I used benecol instead of butter and served the Parmesan on the side.

We really liked this dish! I did sub butternut squash ravioli (so good together) for the pasta because I had it and threw in some broccoli tops to use them up. I mixed the cheese with an egg yolk and stirred that in with a bit of the pasta water to make a sauce. I did sweat the eggplant beforehand and next time will probably use more spinach and cube the eggplant larger, more like 1/2"-3/4". Thank you for a great recipe!

4 people here eat more than 3/4 cup pasta!. More like that amount each. Up to 100g dry pasta per person. I cooked the eggplant in the oven unpeeled (you could maybe use an air fryer). All ingredients as suggested.Good recipe. Might add lemon zest as suggested below next time.

The combination of flavors make this a very tasty dish. I had to supplement the fresh spinach with some frozen but it still came out very good. I only have a few recipes with eggplant and this is the first time I combine it with pasta. I'm so glad I came across this recipe. I will definitely be making it again.
It was ok but not amazing.
Great, tasty dish! Very easy ! Love it!

Wow! I was skeptical but because of the great reviews, I decided to try it. It is delicious and satisfying. I followed the instructions and recipe, but I added a tsp of pesto (as one suggested) and 4 slices of slightly cooked, chopped bacon (just because I wanted to) and about 1/4 cup of Julienne sliced sun dried tomatoes. After tasting it, I couldn't wait to plate it and eat it!

I had an eggplant I didn't know what to do with. For some reason I thought it was a good idea to grow them in the garden not knowing how to cook them. This will work. I need to add more spinach and it probably needed a little bit more oil or butter and lemon juice. What else would be great with some grilled chicken or perhaps shrimp and it's a protein.

LOVED this! Took reviewer advice to sweat the eggplant and upped the garlic, spinach, lemon juice and pasta to taste and to serve more. I also added the garlic after the first 5 mins of cooking the eggplant to preserve its flavor.
I added red pepper flakes, would like to try cheddar shaved, or feta next time.
